stories.title: Rays Win ALCS Game 6 — Headed to the World Series
stories.angle: Tampa Bay beats Cleveland 7-3 in Game 6 at Tropicana Field to advance to the World Series for the third time in franchise history, first since 2020. Freddy Peralta started and allowed just 1 ER over 5.1 IP. Junior Caminero hit a two-run home run in the seventh off the left-field foul pole. Bryan Baker closed with a perfect ninth. Yandy Díaz had publicly promised a win before the game. Rays join the Brewers, making this the first World Series guaranteed to produce a first-time champion in years.

facebook.long_form:
The Tampa Bay Rays are going to the World Series.

After 162 regular-season games and 11 playoff games — after beating the Yankees in the ALDS and pushing past the Guardians in the ALCS — Tampa Bay clinched the American League pennant Monday night with a 7-3 win in Game 6 at Tropicana Field.

It wasn't Drew Rasmussen on the mound for the clincher. It was Freddy Peralta, who gave the Rays 5.1 strong innings and allowed just one earned run. The game turned in the seventh inning, when Junior Caminero crushed a two-run homer off the left-field foul pole to push the lead to 5-1. Bryan Baker handled the ninth without breaking a sweat.

Before the game, Yandy Díaz publicly declared the Rays would win. He was right.

Tampa Bay advances to their third World Series in franchise history and first since 2020. They'll face the Milwaukee Brewers, who swept the Dodgers in the NLCS. Game 1 is Friday, October 23 at American Family Field in Milwaukee.

Neither the Rays nor the Brewers have ever won a World Series. One of them will.

facebook.long_form:
The 2026 World Series is set.

Tampa Bay Rays vs. Milwaukee Brewers. Game 1 is Friday, October 23 at American Family Field in Milwaukee (8PM ET, FOX). The entire series will air on FOX.

Here's what makes this matchup historic: neither franchise has ever won a World Series. The Brewers came closest in 1982, when they fell to the Cardinals in seven games. The Rays appeared in 2008 (lost to the Phillies) and 2020 (lost to the Dodgers in six). Both teams are No. 1 seeds. The team that wins this series will be a first-time champion.

The Brewers were baseball's best team in 2026, winning 103 regular-season games. They swept San Diego in the NLDS and swept the defending champion Dodgers in the NLCS, rallying from a 4-0 deficit in the clinching game. Jake Bauers won NLCS MVP. Jackson Chourio broke the franchise's all-time postseason home run record.

The Rays have been built for October. Drew Rasmussen has a 1.29 ERA in the postseason this year. They beat the Yankees in the ALDS and the Guardians 4-2 in the ALCS.

This is going to be good.

stories.title: Rasmussen vs. Misiorowski — Game 1 Could Be Historic
stories.angle: Game 1 of the World Series will likely feature one of the best pitching matchups of the 2026 postseason. Drew Rasmussen (Rays) is the probable starter — he went 16-5 with a 2.67 ERA in the regular season and has been untouchable in the playoffs (1.29 ERA, 15 IP). Jacob Misiorowski (Brewers) led the NL in ERA and strikeouts in 2026. Both are two-time All-Stars. This is a duel worth circling on the calendar.

facebook.long_form:
If the probable starters hold, Game 1 of the World Series could be one of the best-pitched games you'll see all year.

On the mound for Tampa Bay: Drew Rasmussen. He went 16-5 with a 2.67 ERA in the regular season and has been dominant in the 2026 postseason — 1.29 ERA over 15 innings, including an 8-inning gem against the Yankees in the ALDS where he struck out 10 and allowed just one hit. He's a two-time All-Star.

On the mound for Milwaukee: Jacob Misiorowski. He led the National League in ERA and strikeouts during the regular season, earning his second All-Star selection. He had 12 days of rest heading into the Series.

Neither pitcher has appeared in a World Series game before. Both are arguably at the peak of their careers.

October 23. American Family Field. 8PM ET on FOX. Mark it.

stories.title: Milwaukee's Historic Journey to the Fall Classic
stories.angle: The 2026 Milwaukee Brewers are one of the most dominant teams to ever reach a World Series. They won 103 regular-season games (MLB's best), swept the Padres in the NLDS, and swept the Dodgers — the defending champions — in the NLCS, rallying from 4-0 down in the clinching game. Jake Bauers won NLCS MVP. Jackson Chourio broke the franchise's all-time postseason HR record (6th career postseason HR, breaking the tie with William Contreras). The Brewers' last World Series appearance was in 1982, when they lost to the Cardinals. This is the franchise's chance to finally win the title that has eluded them for 57 years.

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
103 wins. Swept the Padres. Swept the Dodgers.

Milwaukee hasn't hosted a World Series game since 1982.

The Brewers have never won one.

That changes starting Oct. 23. #ThisIsMyCrew

facebook.long_form:
The 2026 Milwaukee Brewers have been special from the start.

They won 103 games during the regular season, the best record in baseball. They swept the San Diego Padres in the NLDS. They swept the Los Angeles Dodgers — the defending World Series champions — in the NLCS, capping their run with an improbable comeback from a 4-0 deficit in Game 4, winning 6-4 at Dodger Stadium.

Jake Bauers was named NLCS MVP. Jackson Chourio hit his sixth career postseason home run, breaking the Brewers' all-time franchise record (the previous holder was William Contreras, his own teammate). Brice Turang drove in 100 runs during the regular season.

The Brewers have never won a World Series. Their last appearance was in 1982 — a seven-game loss to the Cardinals. That was 44 years ago. The franchise has waited a long time for this.

Now they're hosting Game 1 on Friday night at American Family Field, in front of what will be the loudest crowd in Milwaukee sports history.

The wait is almost over.
facebook.image_caption: 🏆 103 wins. Swept the Padres. Swept the Dodgers. The 2026 Brewers are one of the most dominant teams to ever reach a World Series. Friday night, they play for the title. #ThisIsMyCrew #WorldSeries
